column1: # The C libc-ABI scenario, driven by `just test-cabi <arch>`.
# `/bin/cabi` is compiled against `tools/c-include` and linked against the port's
# `minix-libc`, so it is the one program that meets both sides of these ABIs —
# the Rust userland binaries go through `minix-std` and never touch the symbols
# or the struct layouts the headers declare.
# Three phases, each a place where a header and an implementation can drift
#   1. `sockaddr_in` — built from the header, bound, read back through
#      getsockname; the family and port must survive.
#   2. `pipe2(O_NONBLOCK)` — the flag must reach the open file description the
#      pipe's read path consults (VFS `F_SETFL`), so `F_GETFL` reports it and a
#      read on the empty pipe answers EAGAIN instead of blocking.
# One step, asserting the last line: it is printed only after all three passed,
# and each failure prints a diagnostic instead. A single invocation, because
# phase 1 binds a fixed port — a second run in the same boot would race the
